terra.problem: The passage does not say whether the sisters sent a note or spoke privately to a cousin.
The sisters stand before Moses, Eleazar, the leaders, and the congregation. The passage does not say all those people were standing.
Manasseh is the ancestor of the clans to which the sisters belong, not the name of their own clan. The passage also does not say that speaking to relatives would have been easy.
Calling the question a trap comments on the lesson’s question.
The passage does not say the sisters spoke before anyone could whisper about their father.
This passage calls the request property, but does not identify it as land. A fact from outside the passage needs its own reference.
The passage says Moses brought the case before the LORD. It does not say whether he guessed or held a vote.
The LORD tells Moses that the daughters speak correctly. The passage does not say the sisters were told this or that they were not sent away.
The passage says their inheritance is to be transferred to the daughters, but does not say their father’s name stays in the family.
Papa claims he has had debts, adding an unsupported detail to his own story.
The passage calls it property and an inheritance, but does not identify it as a share in the land. A fact from outside the passage needs its own reference.
The passage does not say the LORD made the rule so the family line would keep going. The rule concerns who receives the inheritance.
